@coldplay delivered a historic performance in Ahmedabad, captivating an audience of over 150,000 at the Narendra Modi Stadium (twice), making it their largest concert to date. The British rock band's monumental event was part of their Music of the Spheres India Tour, which had previously seen them perform in Mumbai.

The concert, held on January 25 and 26, transformed the stadium into a luminous spectacle. The band's official X account shared their excitement, expressing gratitude towards the massive turnout and inviting fans to join their next live stream.

Lead singer Chris Martin greeted the crowd in Gujarati, enhancing the local connection by saying, "Tame logo are badha Sundar largo cho. Hu tamare shahar ma aavyo chu. Kem cho Ahmedabad?" which translates to "You all look beautiful. I have come to your city. How are you, Ahmedabad?"

The highlight of the night was a performance of their hit 'A Sky Full of Stars', during which Martin encouraged the crowd to participate, creating a sea of lights and music. The atmosphere was electric, with fireworks illuminating the sky, adding to the visual grandeur of the event.

Social media was abuzz with reactions, capturing videos and images that showcased the scale of the concert. Prominent figures like Anand Mahindra shared moments from the night, emphasizing its significance in global music history. The event was not just a musical act but a cultural bridge, with Coldplay acknowledging Indian icons and historical contexts during their performances.

This concert is not only a testament to Coldplay’s global appeal but also marks India and Ahmedabad’s rising prominence as a host for international music events. Fans left the venue with unforgettable memories, having witnessed a truly global music spectacle right in their city.
